Sorry for back-to-back posts in your journal....I just want to make sure I understand why you took this trade, and I have a follow up question.

Step 1:

It looks like you chose a higher time swap level engulf. Here are the two important zones:

Step 2: Draw all lower time swap zones (fractal levels) within FL Box B. Flag Box D is a medium term true supply zone, but there is a lower time frame true supply zone located just above it...I labeled that FL Box F. Without zooming in to a 1 min chart, it is easy to overlook FL Box F because it just looks like a DP in the 5 min chart. When zoomed in to a 1-min chart, it is obvious that this is also true supply formed after an engulf of a LTF swap zone.

Step 3: Expect price to FO to the FL Box F (which is exactly what happened). All of these smaller FL Boxes exist within the largest (HTF) FL Box B.

My follow up question:

When I see excellent trades like this one you found, I (usually) understand why it worked. My problem is finding these areas on a live chart as price is unfolding. Most of this is a skill learned through continual practice, and will come in time, however I am curious to know what your top down process was for this trade (only if you are willing to share, of course ).

For example, did you see something on a higher time frame (above the 5 min chart) that aided your analysis to take a close look at this zone? Also, before taking this trade, did you ID the most recent downside engulf and target to determine if price was likely to bounce from this level, or was the LTF PA enough confirmation for you?

Maybe I am just lousy at seeing good entries, but often times I see similar setups that get run through with no bounce. Was there any other factor that made you feel more comfortable going short at FL Box F that hasn't already been shown in your trade charts?

Thanks so much!

Hi H, first let me clarify I did not trade this. I posted this after seeing the charts again when staurum posted a chart as I was no longer trading for the day...

The trade I took was this:

OK now to your questions.

You write that many of these levels fail.

Hard to predict which level is going to work unless having IF level reading skills. Also salivan, Omid and others are getting better and better at TT these levels because of their ability to decode ITs intentions and good traps (like fake supply/demand at FL R/S aka "supply/demand created"). But the real clue for the setup above was the reaction and approach.

HTF picture can help but in this case it was not relevant because of the context.

If the market has a fractal nature then the lower stuff should work also if against HTF.

Of course better to go with HTF direction but if the other factors are in alignment then it is still a good setup.

Like I posted above the 10sec EU IT extended FO play, it was against the HTF direction as I was long but at the same time worked nicely while in opposite direction...

As I wrote above, the easiest approach is the way the price reading article says.

First step, identify a possible level, I've seen from your journal that you can dissect HTF FL and find the nested levels, so that's what you need. There's really only one level to look for trades and this is the FL (true supply/demand).

Then the key is to watch the approach if it makes sense and the go/no go is the reaction. If we have an unmet target then it is all we need.

The approach was a big hint:

This webinar from IF is really key for this regarding nested levels with tricks:

Hope this helps
